jobs.prompt: TOP PRIORITY: swarm update rewrites the version field of .project-swarm.json in every linked project (bumpPointers in tools/swarm/core-12.mjs calls writePointer in tools/install.mjs). The file is tracked, so every runner update dirties every project tree and blocks the autopilot and integrate. Fix: the runner version pointer stops living in a tracked file. Design: the tracked .project-swarm.json keeps only project profile data (budget, ui, pin, install path hints that do not change per release). The per-release fields (version, and any field bumpPointers or writePointer changes on update) move to an untracked machine-local file .swarm/runner-pointer.json inside the project (the .swarm folder is already git-ignored or generated state; verify .swarm is ignored by the project .gitignore that init writes, and add the ignore line in init when missing). Every reader of the pointer (find them all: search tools for .project-swarm.json, readPointer, pointer.version, status.mjs, handoff-commands.mjs, scope-commands.mjs, kit.mjs, state-backup.mjs, errors-commands.mjs, init-profile.mjs, security-gate.mjs, pins.mjs, the launcher resolution that picks the runner version) reads the merged view: the local file wins for the per-release fields, the tracked file is the fallback so an old project keeps working. One shared function readRunnerPointer(project) in tools/pins.mjs or a new tools/runner-pointer.mjs does the merge; all readers use it. writePointer on update writes ONLY the local file (atomic temp plus rename, mode 0644) and never touches the tracked file. Migration (one time, automatic on the first update or init after this release, and by swarm doctor if it exists): when the tracked file holds per-release fields, copy them to the local file; then remove those fields from the tracked file ONLY when the tracked file is clean in git (git status --porcelain for that path is empty) and the project is on a non-protected branch... if it is not clean or the branch is protected, leave the tracked file as is and report once (migration-deferred) so no commit is made for the owner. Never run git add or git commit. A pinned project (pin field) stays untouched by update exactly as today; the pin stays in the tracked file because it is a project decision. swarm init for a new project writes the profile to the tracked file and the version to the local file. Tests in tests/runner-pointer.test.mjs, hermetic (temp git repos, temp install roots, no ambient environment): after bumpPointers the tracked file bytes and git status are unchanged and the local file holds the new version; readRunnerPointer merges (local wins, fallback to tracked, both missing handled, corrupt local file handled with a clear message); migration copies fields, strips them from a clean tracked file, defers on a dirty tracked file and on a protected branch, never stages or commits, is idempotent; pinned projects are skipped; init writes the ignore line and is idempotent; every reader call site returns the same version as before for an un-migrated project (status, launcher resolution); the autopilot checkout check passes right after an update. Keep every existing test passing (change a test only where intended behavior changes, with a comment). Never import install.mjs statically from new modules. Tests are hermetic (no ambient environment, no TTY, no network). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.

jobs.prompt: TOP PRIORITY bug report from the owner: on the atlas-seafloor project the hand-build guard now refuses every handbuild command from the orchestrator session, even status and request. Only approve (and the other owner verbs) must be owner-only. A probe of guardDecision at current main allows swarm handbuild status, list, show and request in the plain, --root, cd-prefixed, and node runner forms, so the refusal comes from a path the probe did not cover. Reproduce and fix it. Investigate in order and report which was the cause in the test file header: (a) the PreToolUse hook script path (tools/handbuild-guard.mjs) end to end: feed it real hook payloads (Bash tool input JSON on stdin) for each verb and form, with and without the CLAUDECODE variable, with and without other agent env variables, from the project root and from a worktree and a subfolder, and check its exit code and output; (b) the generated hook the install step writes into a linked project (ensureHandbuildGuard and ensureOrchestratorHooks in tools/install.mjs): a stale hook copy or one that embeds an older decision function or a different command list; (c) the git hooks installed by swarm handbuild install; (d) self-approval.mjs and shell-writes.mjs classifiers treating the word handbuild with a request or status argument as an approval (for example a substring or token match on approve, request id patterns, or flags like --reason text that contains the word approve, deny, on or off inside quotes: a reason string such as approve the commit window must not turn a request into an approval); (e) a project with a space or special characters in its path, a quoted command, env-var prefixes (FOO=1 swarm handbuild status), a pipe or redirect after the command (swarm handbuild status | head), a heredoc, command substitution wrapping, sudo or env or time prefixes, and the full path of the swarm binary (/opt/homebrew/bin/swarm, ~/.local/bin/swarm, ~/.project-swarm/current/tools/swarm.mjs, node with flags before the script); (f) the owner-verb list: exactly approve, deny, on, off, install, uninstall and swarm decide handbuild-ID approve|deny are owner-only; status, list, show, request, log, check and help are allowed; an unknown verb is allowed only when it is read-only by the CLI itself (the CLI refuses unknown verbs on its own), never silently blocked; the bare handbuild command and --help are allowed. Fix the cause(s) found. Whatever the refusal, the message must name the exact matched rule (rule id) and the verb so the next report shows it, and add the rule id to the hook output. Tests in tests/handbuild-guard-verbs.test.mjs, hermetic: a table of every verb times every invocation form in (e) above (allowed verbs allowed, owner verbs blocked), run through guardDecision AND through the hook script with a real payload on stdin, with the orchestrator env set; reason strings containing approve, deny, on, off do not change the verdict of a request; the refusal output includes the rule id; a generated hook in a temp linked project behaves the same as the source hook (refresh brings a stale copy up to date). Keep every existing test passing (change a test only where intended behavior changes, with a comment). Never import install.mjs statically from new modules. Tests are hermetic (no ambient environment, no TTY, no network). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.
